spans.s:
अचक्र अ-चक्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having no wheels;
immoveable; not vacillating; automatous (?).

अचक्षुस् अ-चक्षुस्, उस्, n. a bad or miser-
able eye, no eye; (उस्, उस्, उस्), blind.
—अ-चक्षुर्-
विषय, अस्, आ, अम्, not or no longer within reach of
the eyes, invisible.
—अचक्षुष्-ट्व, अम्, n. blindness.
आ-चक्षुस्, उस्, m. a learned man, a Paṇḍit.
अ-चक्षुष्क, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of eyes, blind.

अचण्ड अ-चण्ड, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, not of a
hot temper, gentle, tractable; (ई), f. a tractable cow.

अचतुर अ-चतुर, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of
four, having less than four; not cunning, not dexterous.
अचन्द्र अ-चन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम्, moonless.

अचपल अ-चपल, अस्, आ, अम्, not oscillating
or vibrating; unmoveable, steady.

अ-चापल्य, अम्, n. freedom from unsteadiness,
firmness.

अचर अ-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, or अ-चरत्, अन्,
अन्ती, अत्, immoveable.

आ-चार, अस्, m. conduct, manner of action; beha-
viour; good conduct, good behaviour; custom, prac-
tice, usage; an established rule of conduct, an ordi-
nance, an institute, a precept; manner of conducting
one's self, diet; rule; [cf. Hib. acara, ‘convenience,
conveniency, use.’]
—आचार-चन्द्रिका, f. title of a
work on the religious customs of the Śūdras.
—आचार-
तन्त्र, अम्, n. one of the four classes of Tantras
with Buddhists.
—आचार-दीप, अस्, m. ‘lamp of re-
ligious customs,’ title of a work.
—आचार-भ्रष्ट,
अस्, आ, अम्, fallen from established usage, apostate.
—आचार-मयूख, अस्, m. ‘ray of religious cus-
toms,’ title of a work.
—आचार-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, well-
conducted, virtuous.
—आचार-वरिजित, अस्, आ, अम्,
irregular, out of rule; outcast.
—आचार-विरुद्ध,
अस्, आ, अम्, contrary to custom.
—आचार-वेदी, f.
‘altar of religious customs,’ a N. of Āryāvarta.
—आ-
चार-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of established ordi-
nances, outcast.
—आचाराङ्ग (˚र-अङ्˚), अम्, n. title
of the first of the twelve sacred books of the Jainas.
—आचारादर्श (˚र-आद्˚), अस्, m. ‘looking-glass
of religious customs,’ title of a work.
—आचारार्क
(˚र-अर्˚), अस्, m. ‘sun of religious customs,’ title of
a work.
—आचारोल्लास (˚र-उल्ल्˚), अस्, m. ‘light of
religious customs,’ title of a work.

अचरम अ-चरम, अस्, आ, अम्, not last, not
least.

अचल अ-चल, अस्, आ, अम्, not staggering or
moving, immoveable; (अस्), m. a mountain or rock;
a bolt or pin; the number seven; N. of Śiva
and of the first of the nine deified persons, called
‘white Balas’ among the Jainas; (आ), f. the earth;
one of the ten earths of the Buddhists.
—अचल-
कीला, f. the earth.
—अचल-त्विष्, ट्, m. the Kokila or
Indian cuckoo.
—अचल-धृति, इस्, f. a metre of four
lines, of sixteen short syllables each, also called
Gītyāryā.
—अचल-भ्रातृ, ता, m., N. of a Brāhman
from Oude, who became one of the eleven heads of
Gaṇas among the Jainas.
—अचल-मति, इस्, m., N.
[]
of a Rākṣasa.
—अचल-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, m. chief of
mountains.
—अचलाधिप (˚ल-अध्˚), अस्, m. (king
of mountains), the Himālaya.
—अचला-सप्तमी, f.
title of a book in the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa.

अचारु अ-चारु, उस्, वी, उ, not pretty, in-
elegant.
आच 1. आच, अस्, m., N. of a man.

आच 2. आच, in the words आच-पराच and
आचोपच, ‘turned towards and away from’ (?).

आचक्ष् आ-चक्ष्, cl. 2. A. -चष्टे, -ष्टुम्, to
look at, inspect; to tell, relate, make a communication
about anything (with acc.); to announce, declare; to
make known, confess; to acquaint, introduce to; to
address any one (with acc.); to call, name.
आ-चक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, saying, declaring.

आचतुरम् आ-चतुरम्, ind. till the fourth
generation.

आचतुर्य आचतुर्य, अम्, n. (fr. अ-चतुर),
clumsiness, stupidity.

आचम् आ-चम्, cl. 1. P. -चामति, -चमितुम्,
to sip; to rinse the mouth (with inst. of the thing);
to lap up, lick up, to cause to disappear (as the wind
licks up moisture): Caus. -चामयति, -यितुम्, to
cause to sip water.
आ-चम, अस्, m. rinsing the mouth.

आ-चाम, अस्, m. sipping water, rinsing the mouth;
the water or foam of boiled rice.

आ-चमन, अम्, n. rinsing the mouth, sipping
water (before religious ceremonies, before meals &c.,
from the palm of the hand. It is usual to spit the
water out again; the ceremony also includes touching
the body in various parts); gargling the throat; the
water used for rinsing the mouth.
आ-चमनक, अस्, m. a spitting pot.
आ-चामनक, अस्, m. a spitting pot.

आचमनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, used for rinsing the
mouth; (अम्), n. water for rinsing the mouth, a
gargle.

आ-चम्य, ind. having rinsed the mouth, having
sipped and ejected a little water.

आ-चाम्य, अम्, n. rinsing the mouth, water so
used, a gargle; (अस्, आ, अम्), to be rinsed.

आ-चान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, sipped and ejected (as water);
one who has rinsed his mouth.
आचान्त, आचाम। See under आ-चम्.
आ-चामक, अस्, आ, अम्, rinsing the mouth.

आचय आ-चय, अस्, m. (fr. rt. चि with आ),
collection, plenty.

आचयक, अस्, आ, अम्, collecting, skilful in col-
lecting.

आचर् आ-चर्, cl. 1. P. ep. A. -चरति, -ते,
-रितुम्, Ved. -रध्यै, -रितवे, -रसे, to come near
to, approach; to step upon, pass through; to pro-
ceed, manage, behave one's self towards (with loc.);
to treat; to have intercourse with, frequent; to act,
undertake, do, exercise, practice, perform; to devour,
eat into; to help forward, put into.
आ-चर्; add — to examine (a witness).

आ-चरण, अम्, n. approaching, arrival; following,
observing, conduct, usage, practice; an institute, rite
or rule of conduct; a cart, carriage.

आ-चरणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be done or performed;
to be followed or observed, right, proper.

आ-चरत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, following, practising, ob-
serving.

आ-चरित, अस्, आ, अम्, observed, practised, as a rite
or usage; usual, customary; enjoined, fixed by rule.

आ-चरितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be performed in a
customary manner; to be done or performed.

आ-चर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be gone to or approached;
to be done or performed.

आ-चार्य, अस्, m. lit. ‘one to whom one must have
recourse’ or ‘one who is to be attended to or waited
on’ or ‘one whose precepts are to be followed’ or
‘one who knows the आचार or rules;’ a spiritual guide
or teacher, especially one who invests the student
with the sacrificial thread, and instructs him in the
Vedas, in the law of sacrifice and religious mysteries
(Manu 2. 140, 171); an epithet of Droṇa the teacher
of the Pāṇḍus; (आ), f. a spiritual preceptress. The
title आचार्य affixed to names of learned men is
rather like our Dr.; e. g. राघवाचार्य, &c.
—आचार्य-करण, अम्, n. acting as teacher.
—आ-
चार्य-ता, f. or आचार्य-त्व, अम्, n. the office or pro-
ficiency of a holy teacher.
—आचार्य-देव, अस्, m.
one whose preceptor is his god.
—आचार्य-भो-
गीन, अस्, आ, अम्, delighting the holy teacher.
—आचार्य-मिश्र, अस्, आ, अम्, venerable, honourable.
—आचार्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has a teacher.
—आचार्योपासन (˚य-उप्˚), अम्, n. waiting upon
or serving the spiritual preceptor.

आचारिक, अस्, ई, अम्, conformable to rule or prac-
tice, prescriptive, authorized; (अम्), n. rules for the
preservation of health, habit of life, regimen, diet.

आचारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, following established rites or
practice.

आ-चारी, f. the plant Hingtsha Repens, also called
Hilamocikā.

आचार्यक, अस्, आ, अम्, originating from a spiritual
teacher; (अम्), n. the proficiency of a holy teacher.
आचार्यानी, f. (with dental न्, Pāṇini
Vārt. 6
), the wife of an Ācārya or holy teacher.

आचरण्य आ-चरण्य (nom. fr. चरण), P.
-चरण्यति, -यितुम्, to move one's self, to move or
extend towards.

आचल् आ-चल्, Caus. P. -चालयति, -यितुम्, to
move, draw away from one's place, stir up.
